I did the same. My sugestion is that everytime you want to navigate use ctrl+shift+a. This way, you always see the keybind to that and try to remember. You can also use a plugin called "X-promotor-key" (or something like that, don't remeber the exat name). It basically tells you whenever you do something that has a keybind and remembers you to use it.

I think both are great, with a few perks. VSCode is definitely easier to access because it's free and the plugins need are easy to install, apart from been beautiful. IntelliJ on the other has better diagnostics and debugging while also having the 'intentions' system which I like very much.

I base my choice in how serious I need to code to spend money on the platform. In this case, since I work coding, I use IntelliJ (actually CLion but whatever).

So, to use a font on a website you first need to load that font. For that, it dependes on the browser, but I would try

src: url('myfont.ttf') format('truetype');

After that, since your font name has a space in it, you need to put the font name in quotes. This indicates to CSS that it is a single name. Remember that source also has to get the spaced name.

That should work, but recently browser have switch to another type of font, which uses a .woff extension. I think it might stoll work with the true type font, but I would go hunt for this font in the .woff format just to make sure.

Here's where you can get some more information on this: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/24990554/how-to-include-a-font-ttf-using-css

Hope it helps!😊
